topSignals.title: Elcogen's China partnership moves from MoU to signed commercial supply agreements — the first MW-level SOC projects for the priority stack player.
topSignals.text: Elcogen and Shanghai HyEnergy Technology Co. Ltd. (published Sept 15) have signed supply agreements for their first MW-level solid oxide projects in China, progressing a relationship that began with a March 2026 MoU, a June 2026 executive visit to Tallinn, and now concrete commercial contracts covering green hydrogen production, CHP and energy storage applications. This is a genuine step-change from partnership-announcement to revenue-generating deployment, not another MoU. Elcogen

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy published a new techno-economic report claiming its 800V DC-native SOFC power can cut non-compute capex for a 1 GW AI data center by $3.6B (27%) and 5-year TCO by $5.5B (9%) versus conventional AC infrastructure — directly LCOE-relevant.
topSignals.text: The claim: Bloom's SOFC generates 800V DC electrochemically on-site with no AC-to-DC conversion stage, cutting transformer/switchgear dependence (previously an FCEL-only differentiator vs. Bloom's AC output — see Aug/July digests). Stock jumped ~5-7% on the report plus a same-week Mizuho price-target raise to $351 (from $242, Sept 14) and the Hitachi-Japan news below; BE closed around $270 today vs. ~$252-253 Tuesday. Caveat: Bloom's own numbers, site-specific in practice. Bloom Energy IR | FuelCellsWorks

topSignals.title: Hitachi and Bloom Energy announced a collaboration to deploy SOFC-based on-site power for data centers and industrial customers in Japan (Sept 2, not previously logged in this monitor).
topSignals.text: Hitachi leads overall planning/design/operational support; Bloom supplies the fuel cell systems. The companies previously demonstrated remote control and monitoring of Bloom's fuel cells via Hitachi's control systems at Hitachi's Omika Works. This opens a new geography (Japan) for SOFC data-center deployment alongside the existing US pipeline, addressing Japan's AI-driven power-demand growth and slow grid-expansion timelines. ESG News | Hydrogen Fuel News

items.text: Elcogen (priority): See Top Signal #1 — first MW-level commercial supply agreements signed with Shanghai HyEnergy (China), a material progression from the August 24 China Southern Power Grid MoU. Status otherwise unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform, ELCO I Tallinn at 360 MW/yr.

Topsoe (priority): Confirmed quiet via direct press-releases check today. Featured items remain the Half-year statement 2026 (already logged Aug 27) and CEO Elena Scaltritti's appointment (already logged, old news). No new SOFC/SOEC announcement. Status unchanged: Herning SOEC-only factory hibernated, SOFC/data-center pathway deferred to 2029+.

Ceres Power: No new stack/cell news. H1 2026 results due before market open Wednesday Sept 23; consensus per Defense World is a loss of ~$0.0644/share on ~$34.75M revenue. This will be the first hard test of the commercial-execution questions raised by Panmure Liberum's June double-downgrade.
No new stack/cell announcements found from FuelCell Energy, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, or Aisin.
Hitachi–Bloom Energy Japan collaboration — see Top Signal #3. New geography for SOFC data-center/industrial on-site power deployment.

Elcogen–Shanghai HyEnergy first MW-level China projects — see Top Signal #1. Applications named: green hydrogen production, CHP, energy storage (not confirmed as data-center-specific, but relevant to the broader SOC commercial-deployment pipeline Dominic is tracking).

Standing pipeline unchanged: Bloom-AEP 1 GW ($2.65B/20yr), Bloom-Brookfield up to $5-25B, Bloom-Nebius $2.6B, Bloom-Equinix >100 MW/19 sites, Bloom-Oracle Project Jupiter up to 2.8 GW, FCEL-Fit Energy up to 380 MW, FCEL's 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement (molten carbonate), FCEL-SDCL up to 450 MW, Ceres-Centrica UK/Europe pipeline, Ceres-Weichai China manufacturing licence.

Bloom Energy (BE): Trading around $270 today (range ~$262-275), up from Tuesday's $252-253 close — see Top Signals #2-3 for drivers (800V DC report, Mizuho PT raise to $351, Hitachi Japan news). S&P 500 inclusion effective before trading Sept 21; securities class-action lead-plaintiff deadline Sept 28; Q3 earnings Oct 27.
Ceres Power (CWR.L): H1 2026 results due Sept 23 (before open); consensus loss ~$0.0644/share on ~$34.75M revenue per Defense World's earnings preview.
FuelCell Energy (FCEL): No new disclosure beyond the already-logged Sept 2 Q3 FY2026 print.

lcoe.text: Bloom Energy's own techno-economic claim (Top Signal #2): 800V DC-native SOFC delivery reduces non-compute capex for a 1 GW AI data center by $3.6B (27%) and 5-year TCO by $5.5B (9%) vs. conventional AC infrastructure, per Bloom's "The New Rules of AI Power" report. Vendor-published, not independently verified — useful as a directional data point on the value of eliminating AC/DC conversion stages, not as a validated LCOE input.

SOFC-GT-Stirling-engine hybrid system (Chen et al., Energy, Vol. 345, published online Jan 27 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.energy.2026.140184):* reports rated energy efficiency 70.7%, exergy efficiency 68.04%, and — operating on natural gas through 2045 — an NPV of $0.0489/kW and LCOE figure of "1050 ($'000)" as reported (units as published; likely a total-cost or normalized figure rather than $/MWh — worth checking the full text before use). Flagged for completeness given no other system papers surfaced this week, not as a directly comparable LCOE benchmark.

Carry-forward, unchanged: Henry Hub last confirmed at $2.81/MMBtu (Sept 9), still below the model's $4.00-4.30/MMBtu assumption — could not independently confirm a more recent EIA print today; Virginia's $0.011/kWh self-generation tax; PJM's $555/MW-day backstop ceiling; US ITC 48E 30% fuel-cell ITC for construction starts after Dec 31, 2025.

Pending calendar: Ceres H1 results (Sept 23), Germany EEG-Novelle first Bundestag reading (Sept 24), Bloom S&P 500 entry (Sept 21), Bloom lead-plaintiff deadline (Sept 28), PJM backstop bid window (Sept 30-Oct 21), Bloom Q3 earnings (Oct 27).
